key_insight: Neuronal ablation produces architecture-dependent language failures: gradual decline in LSTMs, threshold-like collapse from Transformer MLP damage, and smoother decline from attention-head damage.
engineering_relevance: These failure profiles offer a computational damage-tolerance perspective on language-model robustness, rather than evidence about physical fracture or solid mechanics.
method: Systematically ablate computational units in LSTM and Transformer language models.
Compare Transformer MLP ablation with attention-head ablation.
Apply limited fine-tuning as a proxy for compensatory plasticity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports parallel syntactic and semantic decline in LSTMs, semantic substitutions and increasing non-responses after MLP ablation, and reduced semantic specificity after attention-head ablation.
watch_item: Parallels with aphasia and neurodegeneration are qualitative; computational ablation and limited fine-tuning do not establish biological equivalence.
paper_title: Can Language Models Get "Aphasia" From Neuronal Ablation?
